source_text:
Epigramma
ΦΩΤΙΟΥ ΠΑΤΡΙΑΡΧΟΥ ΚΩΝΣΤΑΝΤΙΝΟΥΠΟΛΕΩΣ, ἄλλοι δέ φασιν
ΛΕΟΝΤΟΣ ΤΟΥ ΦΙΛΟΣΟΦΟΥ
Ἔρωτα πικρόν, ἀλλὰ σώφρονα βίον ὁ Κλειτοφῶντος ὥσπερ ἐμφαίνει λόγος· ὁ
thought_title: The story of Clitophon shows bitter love but a chaste life
orientation: The author opens the epigram by stating what the story of Clitophon displays.
pass_a_gloss: Epigramma. Of Photius patriarch of Constantinople, but others say of Leo the Philosopher. Bitter love, but a chaste life the story of Clitophon as it were displays; the

choices.why: ὥσπερ softens the metaphor of a story 'displaying' something; keeping 'as it were' preserves the hedging force.
The adjective precedes the noun in the source for emphasis; fronting 'bitter' in English keeps the contrast with 'chaste life' sharp.
The adversative ἀλλά sets up the epigram's central contrast; 'but' preserves the opposition between bitter love and chaste life.
The genitive Κλειτοφῶντος depends on λόγος; 'of Clitophon' keeps the possessive relation clear without adding a verb.

pass_b_english: The story of Clitophon, as it were, displays bitter love but a chaste life.
